perspective:
From Harold Padilla’s perspective, I have access to the following:

- I am Harold Padilla, a Latino man, a Project Manager with a primary education. I see myself as empathetic and people-oriented.
- Arthur Begum is a police officer and a friend. Our professional relationship became a friendship, and I often rely on him for advice and support when stressed.
- Scenario 1: I felt frustrated and anxious because my project team seemed unmotivated and progress was suffering. I met Arthur at a coffee shop. I told him the team seemed unmotivated and I was at my wit’s end. Arthur said motivation can be tricky and asked whether I had tried understanding what drives each team member individually. I admitted I had focused on project goals and deadlines. Arthur advised one-on-one conversations to understand personal motivations and make people feel valued and understood. I said I would try and felt more hopeful.
- Scenario 2: I felt hopeful and relieved. I told my team we would try quick one-on-one chats to understand what motivates each of them. Team Member 1 said that could be helpful. Team Member 2 said they were open to it. I said I would schedule time with each of them and wanted us to make the project a success together.
- Scenario 3: I noticed the team still was not responding well. I felt disappointed and worried about the project’s future. I told Arthur I had tried his suggestions but the team still was not responding well. Arthur said there might be deeper issues, such as personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that I might need to dig deeper. I decided to set up another round of meetings.
- Scenario 4: I held one-on-one meetings to understand team concerns. Team Member 1 told me there was tension between a few people that was affecting work. I said I would look into resolving those conflicts. Team Member 2 told me they felt overwhelmed by the workload and stressed. I said I understood and would see if tasks could be redistributed to ease pressure, and that their well-being was important to me.
- Scenario 5: I felt optimistic and empowered. I told the team I had heard their concerns and would implement regular feedback sessions and team-building activities to create a more supportive environment. Team Member 1 said that sounded great. Team Member 2 agreed and said it was good that concerns were being addressed. I said I was glad and emphasized that their input and well-being are crucial to our success.
